hero.heading: Upgrade the whole system as one image.
hero.lead: Crustates runs on a read-only, image-based OS. Every update is one signed image. If something breaks, roll back in one step, from the console or the recovery screen.

capabilities.heading: An OS you never have to babysit.

items.title: Read-only root
items.body: The OS can't drift: nothing writes to it at runtime, and composefs verifies every file.

items.title: Atomic upgrades
items.body: A new image is staged next to the running one and applied on reboot. All or nothing.

items.title: One-step rollback
items.body: Boot the previous image from the console, the CLI or the local recovery screen.

items.title: Channels
items.body: Stable and beta channels, with release notes in the console.

items.title: Signed images
items.body: Every image is signed in CI and verified before it is staged.

items.title: Secure and measured boot
items.body: Secure Boot and a TPM-measured boot chain, which also unlocks encrypted disks.

items.title: Offline updates
items.body: Apply an image from a USB stick for air-gapped machines.

items.title: Scheduled windows
items.body: Pick a maintenance window; Crustates drains, upgrades and checks health.

items.title: Kernel and ZFS in lockstep
items.body: Each image ships a pinned kernel with a ZFS module built and tested in CI.

how.heading: Built in CI, verified at boot.
how.lead: Molt images are OCI images built with bootc on Fedora. The same pipeline builds the installer ISO.

steps.title: Build
steps.body: CI builds the image on Fedora with a pinned kernel and the ZFS module, then runs VM-in-CI tests.

steps.title: Sign and publish
steps.body: Images are signed and pushed to the stable or beta channel.

steps.title: Stage
steps.body: Your node pulls the new image into the spare slot and verifies its signature.

steps.title: Boot and check
steps.body: Reboot into it; if health checks fail, it rolls back by itself.

ask.body: "What changes in the next update, and is it safe for my ZFS pool?" The assistant reads the release notes and your setup and summarises the risk.
ask.command: crust ask "what changes in the next update?"

faq.title: Can I install packages on the host?
faq.body: Not on the host itself. Run tools as apps, or build a custom image from ours if you really need to.

faq.title: What if an update breaks my machine?
faq.body: It boots the previous image automatically if health checks fail, or you pick it at boot.

faq.title: How long are releases supported?
faq.body: [PLACEHOLDER]. Stable gets security fixes until the next stable plus a grace period.

faq.title: Is there SSH?
faq.body: Off by default. Turn it on for debugging; everything else goes through the API.
